2M.6 We are to give to God the glory and praise due to his name (the LORD's name is to be praised).

precepts.text: The Most High makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children.
precepts.point: Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
“Is any thing too hard for the Lord?” No. “He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the Lord.”

Sarah, barren from the beginning and past the manner of women, laughed at the thought of having pleasure after she was waxed old. The Most High answered the thought she never spoke, “Wherefore did Sarah laugh”, and when she denied it out of fear He said, “Nay; but thou didst laugh.” He sees what is within the mind, and He makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children.

precepts.text: Praise ye the Lord, O ye servants of the Lord; blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and for evermore.
precepts.point: It was not the mandrakes that gave her the child; it is only coincidence that the baby came after she had them. The Most High is the one who showed her mercy and opened up her womb, for he maketh the barren woman to keep house and to be a joyful mother of children.

note.label: Genesis 30: Trouble in the Flesh and a Righteous Hire

precepts.why:
“Praise ye the Lord. Praise, O ye servants of the Lord, praise the name of the Lord. Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and for evermore.”

That is the answer to Rachel's son. “God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb”, and she said, “God hath taken away my reproach”. It was not the mandrakes that gave her the child; it is only coincidence that the baby came after she had them. The Most High showed her mercy and opened her womb, and the praise for it belongs to His name.

precepts.text: He maketh the barren woman to keep house and to be a joyful mother of children; the Most High is the one who opened Rachel's womb.
precepts.point: It was not the mandrakes that gave her the child; it is only coincidence that the baby came after she had them. The Most High is the one who showed her mercy and opened up her womb, for he maketh the barren woman to keep house and to be a joyful mother of children.

note.label: Genesis 30: Trouble in the Flesh and a Righteous Hire

precepts.why:
“He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the Lord.”

Rachel was barren, and it was not the mandrakes that changed that; it is only coincidence that the baby came after she had them. The Most High is the one who showed her mercy and opened up her womb: “God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb”, and she bare Joseph and said, “God hath taken away my reproach”. He is the one who makes the barren woman a joyful mother of children.

precepts.text: The Most High maketh the barren woman to keep house and to be a joyful mother of children.
precepts.point: This is one of many examples in the Bible of our foremothers going through barrenness, and when the Most High was ready he enabled them to conceive. Sisters who have tried for years without children should in patience possess their souls, take comfort of the scriptures, meditate on the foremothers, and believe what the Bible says.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
The angel told the woman plainly, “thou art barren, and bearest not: but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son.” “He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the Lord.” This is one of many examples in the Bible of our foremothers going through barrenness, and when the Most High was ready he enabled them to conceive.

Sisters who have tried for years without children should in patience possess their souls, take comfort of the scriptures, meditate on the foremothers, and believe what the Bible says: he maketh the barren woman a joyful mother of children.
